cards.explanation: The answer is eight hundred, friends. Josheb-basshebeth, chief of the Three, wields his spear against eight hundred men and kills them at one time (2 Samuel 23:8). That's the number the writer gives. I've stamped some big batches in my day, but I've never had to count to eight hundred and keep a straight face.

The answer is that Eleazar stands his ground and fights. Eleazar son of Dodo stands his ground and strikes the Philistines until his hand grows weary and sticks to his sword (2 Samuel 23:10). The men of Israel are retreating, and he plants his feet anyway. I can barely hold a stamp for a whole batch, and this man's hand wouldn't let go of a sword.

The answer is the LORD, friends. The verse says, "The LORD brought about a great victory that day." Eleazar stood his ground and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and stuck to his sword. Even so, the credit goes to the LORD.
The word is plunder, bakers. The verse says the troops returned to Eleazar, "…but only to plunder the dead." They came back for that and nothing more. I have a feeling Eleazar's sticky hand noticed.

The answer is True. When the Philistines banded together near a field full of lentils, Israel's troops fled from them (2 Samuel 23:11). That's the third mighty man in a row facing a scary crowd. Shammah son of Agee the Hararite is about to show what he does when others run.

The answer is right in the middle of the field, friends. Shammah "…took his stand in the middle of the field…" (2 Samuel 23:12). The troops have fled, and he takes his stand anyway. Lentils all around his ankles, and he's not budging.

The answer is False. Shammah took his stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines, so the Philistines don't take it. The verse ends, "So the LORD brought about a great victory." (2 Samuel 23:12). One man, one field, and the LORD brought the win.

The answer is Bethlehem, friends. David is in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines is at Bethlehem (2 Samuel 23:14). Keep that town in mind, because the next verse is about a well by its gate. It's a long way from the kitchen, but it's the center of this whole story.

The answer is break through. The three mighty men "…broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David." (2 Samuel 23:16). David only wished out loud, and they broke through a whole camp to answer it. I've had people bring me a drink of water, but never through a camp.

The answer is False, bakers. The three men bring the water back, and David "…refused to drink it…" (2 Samuel 23:16). He pours it out to the LORD instead. After all that effort, turning it down is the surprise.

The answer is that David pours it out to the LORD. David refused to drink it and "…poured it out to the LORD…" (2 Samuel 23:16). He doesn't give it back or keep it. I think he's treating that water as something special.

The answer is that his men risked their lives for it, and David says so himself: "Is this not the blood of the men who risked their lives?" (2 Samuel 23:17). He wished for the water, but he won't drink what cost his men that much. I think that tells us how David sees the three who went.

The answer is Joab, friends. Abishai son of Zeruiah is the brother of Joab (2 Samuel 23:18), and Joab son of Zeruiah was over David's army (2 Samuel 8:16). Two brothers, both in David's story. That's a lot of family on one list.

The answer is three hundred, bakers. Abishai wields his spear against three hundred men, kills them, and wins a name along with the Three (2 Samuel 23:18). That's fewer than Josheb-basshebeth's eight hundred, and still plenty to get a name on the list.

The answer is a lion! Benaiah, a man of valor from Kabzeel, goes down into a pit on a snowy day and kills a lion (2 Samuel 23:20). A pit, a lion and snow all in one verse. That's three things I'd avoid in a single day.

The answer is True, friends. Even though the Egyptian is a huge man with a spear in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club (2 Samuel 23:21). A club against a spear sounds like a bad deal on paper. Benaiah goes anyway.

The answer is that Benaiah snatches the spear and uses it! He "…snatched the spear from his hand, and killed the Egyptian with his own spear." (2 Samuel 23:21). The Egyptian had a spear in his hand, and Benaiah went against him with a club. In the end, it was the Egyptian's own spear that settled it.

The answer is False, bakers. Benaiah "…was most honored among the Thirty, but he did not become one of the Three." (2 Samuel 23:23). He still wins a name along with the three mighty men (2 Samuel 23:22). Honored, just not one of the Three.

The answer is his guard, friends. The verse says, "And David appointed him over his guard." (2 Samuel 23:23). Benaiah isn't one of the Three, but David still puts him in charge of something important.
